name: Lo-Hi
description: Finding new drugs is getting harder and harder. One of the hopes of drug discovery is to use machine learning models to predict molecular properties. That is why models for molecular property prediction are being developed and tested on benchmarks such as MoleculeNet. However, existing benchmarks are unrealistic and are too different from applying the models in practice. We have created a new practical \emph{Lo-Hi} benchmark consisting of two tasks: Lead Optimization (Lo) and Hit Identification (Hi), corresponding to the real drug discovery process. For the Hi task, we designed a novel molecular splitting algorithm that solves the Balanced Vertex Minimum $k$-Cut problem. We tested state-of-the-art and classic ML models, revealing which works better under practical settings. We analyzed modern benchmarks and showed that they are unrealistic and overoptimistic. Review: https://openreview.net/forum?id=H2Yb28qGLV Lo-Hi benchmark: https://github.com/SteshinSS/lohi_neurips2023 Lo-Hi splitter library: https://github.com/SteshinSS/lohi_splitter
typical_sota_score: AUC ~0.70–0.95 (Hi); RMSE varies by dataset and endpoint (dataset-dependent)
reputation: Introduced at NeurIPS 2023; recognized as a more realistic, practical benchmark for molecular property prediction but not yet as widely adopted as MoleculeNet.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on cheminformatics; uses realistic train/test splits (novel Hi splitter) to reduce overoptimism in prior benchmarks; moderate dataset sizes and potential dataset-specific label imbalance/contamination risks.
